title: Picnic camps and Bechet as a boy listening outside
summary: Sunday picnic dance halls on the water where several bands played, and young Bechet listening outside, unable to get hired.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now, like you take like Spanish folk, Millen Boy, on Sundays, you see. All them little camps out there, they have bands. They give picnics, you know. You got a band, this, you got a band. It'll be five or six bands. And you get in them camps, you know. And we used to go to the windows, stick our horns out the windows. Toot that that guy, where were there? Across the water, you know. Well, I used to be there, used to be a devil of a time. Get out there nine o'clock in the morning, play till six. And they have the balls out there, more beer. And we blew it.
Was this in somebody's house or were these little...

No, they rent those cabins, you know, where they have a dance. A little dance hall night. Uh-huh. See, they rent them out there on the wharf, you know. Picnic grounds, you know. Picnic clubs, you know.

Some of them used to get them on Saturday night, be out there all night and did. Then, you know, we catch a band out there, you know, and brought one another, you know. Basia used to come out there, sit on the track, but he's out there listening, looking, you know. Wanted to try to get in, you know. See, they wouldn't get high, Basia, you know. They wouldn't hire him? Basia would get drunk, raise some much sand, you know. He was drinking out there? A young boy, too. He'd be sitting out there, he wouldn't have no horn. He'd want to come in and blow something, you know. Yeah. Sometimes, you know. Mm-hmm .
